newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US move toward insurance talks, no date yet.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US move toward insurance talks, no date yet.

text.p: Japan and the United States are moving towards resuming bilateral insurance talks, but have not discussed a date as of yet, Japan's Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
"We have not started any specific discussions," said Ogawa, when asked about the likely date for reopening the talks.

U.S. trade negotiator Ira Shapiro and Eisuke Sakakibara, head of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, agreed in Washington on Wednesday to seek early resumption of the insurance talks, he said, adding that there had been no progress since late July on how to open up Japan's insurance market.
A round of marathon negotiations took place in Vancouver, British Columbia, in late July to resolve the dispute by the end of the month deadline, but no agreement was reached.

Late on Thursday, a senior finance ministry official said the insurance talks will likely be resumed later this month, but added it remains unclear if the two nations would be able to start working-level negotiations next week.
"It would be tough negotiations," the senior ministry official said. He added the two sides have not set a fresh target date for reaching an agreement on the issue.
